A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MiniLM cross-encoder interpretability study despite the changed title. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original activation/path-patching experiments, ablations, IDF interventions, regression evaluations, and downstream model-editing experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds analyses of IDF-dependent attention and separation between IDF and matching signals.

M1.justification: The analyzed model, identified circuit components, patching method, SVD-based editing procedure, and linear approximation remain unchanged. Appendix F adds diagnostic tests of the existing mechanism.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MS-MARCO diagnostic tasks, twelve BEIR datasets, unsafe-token injection scenario, and NFCorpus fine-tuning task. The new analyses reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: BM25 and random-feature regression remain the Table 2 comparators. The same four fine-tuning conditions move from v2 Appendix F.2 to v3 Section 6.4 without comparator changes.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds attention measurements at head 10.1 under IDF scaling, correlations between IDF and Matching Scores, and patching into scoring-head query vectors. Existing splits, sample counts, and fine-tuning budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix F checks the intermediate attention response to IDF editing and whether Matching Heads already carry IDF-weighted signals. These extend the mechanism validation; the earlier ablations, saturation and length analyses, and downstream experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same mean-and-SD reporting, correlation significance reporting, and three-seed fine-tuning description. The new correlation result follows the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Appendix F newly reports an average IDF–Matching Score correlation of r=0.143 (p<0.01), almost no score change from patching into scoring-head query vectors, and attention responses to IDF edits in Figure 14. Existing numerical results, including Table 2 and downstream application scores, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The BM25 formula, SVD decomposition, and linear circuit formalization remain unchanged. The new walkthrough illustrates existing mathematics, while Appendix F supplies empirical checks rather than new formal assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of a semantic BM25-like circuit, localized matching and IDF components, and potential for targeted model editing. The rewritten abstract emphasizes the two-stage interpretation already present in v2.

C2.justification: Appendix F explicitly interprets IDF effects through attention allocation and argues that Matching Scores have little dependence on IDF, supporting separate signal pathways. The limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F specifies the attention readout at head 10.1, explains its selection, and identifies query vectors as the receivers in the added patching check. Existing implementation disclosures and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work section are unchanged, including the relationship to Chen et al. (2024) and the claimed first causal identification of a neural IR relevance circuit.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: it rewrites the abstract, expands Discussion into four subsections incorporating former Appendix F, adds a circuit walkthrough, and reorganizes the appendices. Most core methodological prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially reorganized: downstream plots move into the main discussion, detailed path-patching heatmaps are grouped at the appendix end, and new Figures 10 and 14 provide a circuit walkthrough and IDF-attention plots. Original plots and tables are retained, with several captions expanded.

improvement.justification: Appendix F adds focused evidence for the proposed IDF pathway and its separation from matching signals, while the walkthrough and reorganized discussion make the mechanism easier to assess. These are useful but limited gains: benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the conflicting main-text and appendix descriptions of document-length effects remain unresolved.
